title: arxiv_2505.12854v1
universal_lens: A mathematical framework unifying pose estimation and hold usage detection through joint-keypoint overlap metrics in climbing datasets. Camera positioning and climber diversity define dataset integrity through geometric and kinematic constraints.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian inference models map climber pose states to hold usage via probabilistic keypoint overlap likelihoods, enabling scalable performance analysis. Bayesian inference models climber motion using annotated extremity-hold interactions with probabilistic occlusion estimates.
gse_mapping: Situationally grounded state transitions model climber dynamics across holds using temporal keypoint trajectories and spatial hold geometry. Situational reasoning maps hold usage transitions via state-space traversal of climber extremities and route geometry.

primitives.assumptions: Climber motion is captured at regular temporal intervals; hold usage is binary per time step.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When joint keypoints do not overlap with hold bounding boxes.

layer2.telemetry: Temporal hold activation rate and overlap area ratio

The proposed framework integrates pose estimation accuracy with hold usage semantics, forming a basis for future research in AI-driven climbing technologies. reasoning_traces.think: The chapter introduces four sovereign primitives that quantify different aspects of pose estimation performance in climbing analysis. Primitive w3_missing_detection_rate formalizes the concept of frames lost in tracking, providing a direct measure of temporal gaps in data collection. The primitive w3_pose_sensitivity captures the trade-off between false negatives and false positives inherent in any detection system, aligning with receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Key insight: sensitivity exceeding precision indicates a conservative model that prioritizes recall over specificity, which is desirable for safety-critical applications like assistive technologies for visually impaired climbers. Primitive w3_keypoint_reliance_impact mathematically links geometric properties of bounding boxes to misclassification rates, revealing that larger areas increase the risk of including background clutter. This connects to kernel density estimation in statistics, where bandwidth selection balances bias and variance. Finally, primitive w3_hold_accuracy offers a holistic evaluation metric combining both correct positive and negative predictions, analogous to balanced accuracy in imbalanced classification tasks. Together, these operators form a rigorous framework for assessing and improving computer vision models in sports biomechanics, enabling systematic performance benchmarking and guiding algorithm selection.
